content.text: {"what_it_is": {"claims": [{"text": "F-22A Squadrons (program element 0207138F) is a U.S. Air Force research-and-development program funded in the Research, Development, Test and Evaluation, Air Force account.", "citation": {"fact_id": "82abd0ccef35069e"}}, {"text": "The program funds the modernization of the F-22 Raptor, a multi-mission fighter aircraft that combines low observability, supercruise, maneuverability and integrated avionics to provide air superiority to the Joint Force, access in highly contested environments, and homeland and cruise missile defense.", "citation": {"fact_id": "adf8b481ee2db5e2"}}, {"text": "The F-22 modernization enterprise develops, tests, and fields hardware and software for the air vehicle, engine, Operational Flight Program (OFP), and training systems to improve the jet's weapons, communications, navigation, pilot-vehicle interface, and electronic warfare suite.", "citation": {"fact_id": "adf8b481ee2db5e2"}}, {"text": "The program's Infrastructure effort funds the F-22 Combined Test Force (CTF) at Edwards Air Force Base, California — the only developmental test capability for the entire F-22 enterprise — along with system integration laboratories that plan and conduct development, integration, and verification of Operational Flight Programs and modernization efforts.", "citation": {"fact_id": "7c6b82e743a9c711"}}, {"text": "Modernization thrusts include Sensor Systems, which matures advanced Infrared Search & Track (IRST) capability to preserve first-look, first-shot, first-kill air superiority.", "citation": {"fact_id": "618f38e6d8e60d8f"}}, {"text": "The program funds resilient navigation upgrades, including a Controlled Reception Pattern Antenna (CRPA) to replace the F-22's legacy Fixed Reception Pattern Array antenna and reduce an adversary's ability to jam GPS signals, and Embedded GPS/Inertial Navigation System Modernization (EGI-M) to deliver an M-Code-compliant, anti-spoofing positioning solution.", "citation": {"fact_id": "c2dd42a06b147b61"}}, {"text": "New FY2026 major thrusts include Hybrid SATCOM, which increases the F-22's beyond-line-of-sight capability through commercial and government satellite communications, and the Helmet Mounted Display Cueing System (HMDCS), which lets pilots quickly acquire and designate off-boresight targets.", "citation": {"fact_id": "97288ac3ec336e05"}}]}, "why_it_matters": {"claims": [{"text": "The program's total funding rises from $758,754 thousand (about $759 million) in FY2025 to $852,332 thousand (about $852 million) requested for FY2026.", "citation": {"fact_id": "22dbeee1f196e6b1"}}, {"text": "That is a year-over-year increase of $93,578 thousand (about $94 million) from FY2025 to FY2026.", "citation": {"fact_id": "6e1f23c1ad6ff45f"}}, {"text": "In FY2024 the program recorded actual spending of $640,109 thousand (about $640 million), so the FY2026 request is roughly a third higher than that recent execution level.", "citation": {"fact_id": "7e2898e735bb7908"}}, {"text": "The entire FY2026 request of $852,332 thousand is discretionary funding; the program element carries no reconciliation (mandatory) request for FY2026.", "citation": {"fact_id": "ac98c8dead18ee2c"}}, {"text": "Essentially all of the FY2026 money flows through the single named F-22 project, funded at $852.332 million for the budget year.", "citation": {"fact_id": "4b10a773a9a003ab"}}, {"text": "The FY2026 request was reduced by $1.977 million for Advisory and Assistance Services to promote efficiencies in alignment with Executive Order 14222, the President's Department of Government Efficiency Cost Efficiency Initiative.", "citation": {"fact_id": "adf8b481ee2db5e2"}}]}, "players": {"claims": [{"text": "The program is run by the U.S. Air Force, with funding drawn from the Research, Development, Test and Evaluation, Air Force appropriation.", "citation": {"fact_id": "ac98c8dead18ee2c"}}, {"text": "The F-22 Combined Test Force at Edwards Air Force Base, California, serves as the sole developmental test capability for the entire F-22 enterprise, conducting full-up weapons system and modernization testing.", "citation": {"fact_id": "7c6b82e743a9c711"}}, {"text": "Cryptographic Modernization work updates F-22 radios to meet interoperability and security requirements mandated by the Second Generation Anti-Jam Tactical UHF Radio for NATO (SATURN) specification and by guidance from the National Cryptographic Solution Management Office.", "citation": {"fact_id": "3bbc1d5dbb2f56ce"}}]}, "recent_developments": {"claims": []}}
